differences.what: Maximum request body size differs, which changes when a large body binds to null and hits the guard
differences.lan: Web.config:54 <httpRuntime targetFramework="4.5"/> with no maxRequestLength (default 4096 KB) and no requestLimits (IIS default 30,000,000 bytes)
differences.sap: Web.config:94 maxRequestLength="51200" (50 MB) and :102 maxAllowedContentLength="52428800"
differences.evidence: The comment at SS Web.config:93 says the 50 MB limit is for Base64 uploads (selfies and receipts), meaning other endpoints, not setOrder. No runbook decision covers it. It cannot be reached through the DMZ: the DMZ keeps the default 4096 KB (DMZ Web.config:43) and rejects oversized bodies first, then forwards a re-serialized body of about the same size.
differences.decision_ref: None in the runbook. The setting is deliberate for other endpoints (SS Web.config:93), and its effect on order/new is incidental.
differences.concrete_case: A direct POST (bypassing the DMZ) of a valid 10 MB OrderRequest JSON. LAN fails before the action runs: the exact status is NO EVIDENCE, since it depends on where ASP.NET throws 'Maximum request length exceeded' (the parameter binds to null and returns 400 via :141-142, or the host returns 500). ServicioSAP binds it and processes the order.

differences.what: Bound model shape differs. It does not change the null/400 decision, but it is where silent value differences start
differences.lan: LAN Models/OrderRequest.cs:12-20: subTotal/total/impuesto/costoEnvio are string; articulos is List<Dictionary<string,string>> and infoCliente is Dictionary<string,string>, so raw values and unknown keys are kept and key lookups are case-sensitive
differences.sap: SS Models/SAP/Order/OrderRequest.cs:12,13,17,21 are decimal; ArticuloRequest.cs:7,9,11,13 are decimal/int (cantidad int); InfoClienteRequest.cs:45,69 are int (idMagento, uen). Unknown keys are dropped, and property names match case-insensitively
differences.evidence: Neither controller reads ModelState (grep: no ModelState use in either OrdersController.Set or OrderController.SetOrder). A type conversion error is therefore recorded, marked handled by the formatter, and the property is left at its default. It never yields a null order or a 400 on either side, so the guard behaves the same. The DMZ binds with the LAN-shaped model (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:16-24) and forwards every articulos/infoCliente value as a JSON string. The real credit payloads convert cleanly: CRED515773 has "cantidad":"1" and "precio":"8198.0000"; CRED515848 has "costoEnvio":"150" (magento_payloads.md:26, :55). Runbook §20.3 already acknowledges the costoEnvio case ('Igualarlo exige cambiar el tipo del modelo') as found but not applied, so it is not a decision.
differences.decision_ref: Runbook §20.3 (acknowledged, not decided)
differences.concrete_case: The DMZ forwards articulos:[{"sku":"OSTE00443","cantidad":"1.0000",...}] or "total":"". LAN gets order.articulos[0]["cantidad"]=="1.0000" and total=="". ServicioSAP gets cantidad==0 and total==0 with no error. Neither returns 400, and the effect shows up in later steps.

differences.what: How a downstream 400 would reach Magento through the DMZ (theoretical, cannot happen today)
differences.lan: LAN era: DMZ Curl.Post (DMZ Helper/Curl.cs:108-111) returned e.ToString() for a 400 from LAN. The now-commented check `!response.ToUpper().StartsWith("C")` (DMZ OrdersController.cs:170-175) then answered 500 'Respuesta inesperada'.
differences.sap: Now: DMZ Curl.PostSAP (Curl.cs:130-139) turns a 400 from ServicioSAP into the string 'WebException: ... (400) Bad Request. Body: ', and DMZ returns it as HTTP 200 (OrdersController.cs:214-227).
differences.evidence: Cannot happen through the DMZ, because the DMZ only forwards after its own null guard (:111-112) and always sends JsonConvert.SerializeObject of a non-null object (:196). That object is a JSON object root, which never binds to null in either LAN or ServicioSAP. The DMZ changes are documented as migration choices at DMZ :168-169 and :185-190.
differences.decision_ref: DMZ OrdersController.cs:168-169 and :185-190 migration comments (not a runbook section)
differences.concrete_case: Only if a downstream guard fired while being called through the DMZ: Magento would get 500 in the LAN era and 200 with a 'WebException...' string today. Today the DMZ answers 400 itself before forwarding, in both eras.

comparisons.question_for_user: Does anything other than the DMZ call LAN order/setOrder or ServicioSAP order/new directly (POS, internal tools, test scripts)? The only observable differences in this step (route name, 4 MB vs 50 MB body limit) show up only for direct callers. Through the DMZ the null-body 400 comes from DMZ OrdersController.cs:111-112 and is identical.

comparisons.name: Log of the incoming order body (setOrder, credit path)
comparisons.lan_source: File C:\inetpub\wwwroot\log\setOrder.log on the LAN host (LAN Helper/Logger.cs:19-27). No SQL table or SP is involved. The only code that reads it back is ReSetPedido (LAN Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:1688-1709), called from GET order/getOrderInfoAndSet/{incrementId}.
comparisons.lan_detail:
LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:137-160, Set(OrderRequest) on route order/setOrder:
- :141-142: a null body returns 400 before anything is logged.
- :144: Logger.SetOrder("INFO [" + order.incrementId + "] ", JsonConvert.SerializeObject(order)). This runs OUTSIDE the try, before SetPedido. It is Newtonsoft with default settings, so nulls are kept, applied to the bound LAN OrderRequest (Models/OrderRequest.cs:6-29: 20 properties, all prices as string, infoCliente as Dictionary<string,string>, so every key Magento sends is kept).
- Logger.SetOrder (Helper/Logger.cs:19-27) appends "[yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss] " + type + message with File.AppendText and has NO try/catch. If the write fails (folder missing, file locked, no ACL), the exception leaves the action and LAN answers HTTP 500 without processing the order.
- Resulting line: "[2026-09-25 10:00:00] INFO [CRED515773] {\"entityId\":\"515773\",...}".
- Companion line :152, inside the try: after SetPedido it logs the response, or "No se gener  el pedido, revisa el log SetOrder" when null. The catch (:154-157) logs nothing and returns Ok(e.ToString()).
- The credit branch is not special-cased: every non-null body is logged.

Consumer of the log:
- ReSetPedido (Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:1688-1709) runs File.ReadAllLines on the same path (:1690).
- :1692 takes the first line that contains incrementId and "] INFO [". :1694-1695 returns "no existe" when there is none.
- :1697-1698 cuts everything before the first "{" and deserializes an OrderRequest.
- :1700-1704: if obtenerIdVenta != 0 and esCancelado == 0, it returns "No cumple las condiciones".
- :1706 forces forzarOrder = "1" and :1708 calls SetPedido again.
- Called from Conn/Magento.cs:361-366 (getOrderInfoAndSet). On "no existe", that method falls back to curl.Get("order/jsonOrders/" + incrementId) through the DMZ (:368) and then SetPedido (:404).
- Exposed as GET order/getOrderInfoAndSet/{incrementId} (Controllers/OrdersController.cs:436-443).
- LAN ValidateCredit (:457-482) logs only entityId and incrementId, not the body. Its DMZ forwarder is commented out (DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:366-402), so Magento cannot reach it.
comparisons.sap_source: No equivalent in ServicioSAP. The body is still logged one hop earlier by the DMZ bridge: DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:114 writes to setOrder.log and :194 writes to sap.log, both on the DMZ host, before the forward to ServicioSAP order/new at :196. ServicioSAP only writes C:\inetpub\wwwroot\log\sap.log and {AppBase}\Logs\sap.log (SS Helpers/Logger.cs:8-45), and only when there is an error. ServicioSAP has no replay endpoint.
comparisons.sap_detail:
SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:16-48, SetOrder on route order/new:
- :20-23: a null body returns 400, same as LAN.
- There is NO log before or after SetOrderAsync on the success path (:24-35).
- The only log is in the catch, :45: Logger.SAP("[ORDER NEW ERROR] ", $"incrementId={order?.incrementId} :: {e}"). It records the incrementId and the full exception, not the body. :46 returns Ok("Error, " + e.Message).

SS Methods/Order/OrderMethods.cs:1728-1953, SetOrderAsync:
- The credit branch (:1784-1806) has no Logger.SAP at all, only Console.WriteLine at :1801. It returns at :1802-1806.
- The only payload log, "[SAP ORDER REQUEST]" at :1871, is the SAP sales-order JSON of the cash path. Credit never reaches it.
- Errors in ProcessCreditPaymentAsync are rethrown (:761-765), wrapped at :1950-1953, and reach the controller catch.

No global body logging:
- App_Start/WebApiConfig.cs:11-23 only adds TokenValidationHandler, which does no logging.
- A grep of SS (excluding obj/ and Fakes) for getOrderInfoAndSet, ReSetPedido, jsonOrders, setOrder.log, ReadAllLines and ReadLines finds 0 hits.

SS Helpers/Logger.cs:
- :12-23: the stage/production write is wrapped in a silent try and runs only if the folder exists.
- :28-31: Directory.CreateDirectory({AppBase}\Logs) is OUTSIDE any try, so Logger.SAP itself can throw.
- Evidence in SS Logs/sap.log: 12 lines, none of them a credit order or [ORDER NEW ERROR], so there is no runtime evidence for this step.

What covers the step today, the DMZ (DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:107-228):
- :114: Logger.SetOrder("INFO [" + incrementId + "] ", JsonConvert.SerializeObject(order)). Same format and file name as LAN :144. Present since commit 871eeb7 (2021-05-25). Its logger (DMZ Helper/Logger.cs:8-13) also has no try/catch.
- :194: Logger.SAP("ORDER_BODY_MAGENTO [" + incrementId + "] ", ...), added by commit 50afd93 (2026-07-17), "Migracion SAP - Se añaden logs para los body de Magento en DMZ". It uses a silent try (DMZ Logger.cs:36-48).
- :196: the forward PostSAP("order/new", ...) sends the same serialization.
- :197-198: the SS response is logged.
- The DMZ OrderRequest (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:10-34) has exactly the same 20 properties, types and order as the LAN one. So the DMZ :114 line is byte-identical to what LAN :144 wrote, apart from the timestamp.

Hosts, from config: DMZ Web.config:18 URL_SAP = https://kdll3fhcyo-lan.grupomavi.com/SAP/ and :16 (commented out) URL_INTELISIS = https://kdll3fhcyo-lan.grupomavi.com/api/. That suggests SS and LAN share the LAN host, and the DMZ log sits on a different host. The deployed configuration is NO EVIDENCE.

differences.what: The incoming body is no longer logged on the service that processes the order
differences.lan: LAN :144 writes '[ts] INFO [<incrementId>] <json>' to setOrder.log on the LAN host for every non-null setOrder request, before any processing, whatever the payment method
differences.sap: SS order/new writes nothing on success (OrderController.cs:24-35; credit branch OrderMethods.cs:1784-1806). The same body line still exists one hop earlier: DMZ :114 (setOrder.log) and :194 (sap.log) on the DMZ host, with identical content because the DMZ and LAN models are identical
differences.decision_ref: No runbook decision covers it. Sections 9, 10, 15-18, 20 and 21 say nothing about the body log. Commit 50afd93 in the DMZ ('Se añaden logs para los body de Magento en DMZ') suggests the migration moved this log to the DMZ on purpose, but the user never recorded that as a decision
differences.evidence: LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:144; LAN Helper/Logger.cs:19-27; SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:24-47; SS Methods/Order/OrderMethods.cs:1784-1806; SS App_Start/WebApiConfig.cs:17; DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:114,:194; DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:10-34 vs LAN Models/OrderRequest.cs:6-29
differences.concrete_case: POST the CRED515773 payload (magento_payloads.md, omnipro_pago_credito). LAN appends '[2026-09-25 10:00:00] INFO [CRED515773] {"entityId":"515773","incrementId":"CRED515773",...}' to the processing host's setOrder.log. ServicioSAP appends nothing to either sap.log. The line exists only on the DMZ host. If the same payload is POSTed directly to SS order/new (Postman, local test), the body is recorded nowhere.

differences.what: The replay consumer of the log (ReSetPedido / getOrderInfoAndSet) has no equivalent, and the legacy one is still live
differences.lan: GET order/getOrderInfoAndSet/{id} re-reads the setOrder.log line, forces forzarOrder='1' and calls SetPedido again. If the order is already recorded and not cancelled it returns 'No cumple las condiciones'. If the line is missing it falls back to Magento order/jsonOrders through the DMZ
differences.sap: No endpoint in SS replays a stored body (0 grep hits). The only way to replay is to re-POST to DMZ setOrder or SS order/new, and for credit that creates a second application, because the SD36 duplicate check never finds credit orders (runbook 18.5 #17). The LAN endpoint is still deployed, and after the cutover LAN's setOrder.log gets no new body lines, because the DMZ forward to LAN is commented out (DMZ :133-183)
differences.decision_ref: None. Runbook 18.5 #17 ('Un reintento del mismo CRED crea otra solicitud') is tracked as 'Fuera del fin de semana' and is not decided
differences.evidence: LAN Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:1688-1709; LAN Conn/Magento.cs:361-404; LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:436-443; DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:133-183 (commented); SS grep = 0 hits; SS OrderMethods.cs:1752 (duplicate check before the credit branch)
differences.concrete_case: CRED515773 fails in SS after the cutover. An operator calls LAN GET order/getOrderInfoAndSet/CRED515773. ReSetPedido returns 'no existe' because the line is not in LAN's log. getOrderInfoAndSet then pulls the order from Magento and runs LAN SetPedido, which creates the credit application through the legacy path, not through ServicioSAP. SS has no tool that does the same, and re-POSTing the DMZ-logged body to order/new with forzarOrder '0' or '1' inserts another application.

differences.what: Failure mode when the log cannot be written before processing
differences.lan: Logger.SetOrder at :144 is outside the try and has no internal try/catch. If C:\inetpub\wwwroot\log is missing, locked or not writable, LAN setOrder returns HTTP 500 and creates nothing
differences.sap: SS has no pre-processing log, so a log-folder problem on the SS host cannot block the order. The DMZ :114 keeps LAN's failure mode (Logger.SetOrder without try, before the forward), so through Magento and the DMZ the result is the same. It differs only on the processing host
differences.decision_ref: None
differences.evidence: LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:144 (outside try :149-158); LAN Helper/Logger.cs:23-26; SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:24-35; DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:114; DMZ Helper/Logger.cs:8-13
differences.concrete_case: On the processing host, C:\inetpub\wwwroot\log\ is missing (or setOrder.log is locked). Legacy chain: LAN throws DirectoryNotFoundException at :144, returns 500, and no credit application is written. New chain: SS processes CRED515773, writes the application, and returns 200 {BP, SalesDocument, Message, Resultado:'Concluido'}. If the folder is missing on the DMZ host instead, both chains return 500 at DMZ :114.

differences.what: ServicioSAP adds an error log that LAN does not have, and that log can turn the 200 contract into a 500
differences.lan: The catch (:154-157) logs nothing and always returns HTTP 200 Ok(e.ToString())
differences.sap: The catch logs Logger.SAP('[ORDER NEW ERROR] ', incrementId + full exception) at :45 before returning Ok('Error, ' + e.Message). Logger.SAP calls Directory.CreateDirectory({AppBase}\Logs) outside any try (Logger.cs:28-31). If that throws, the exception leaves the catch block and the caller gets HTTP 500 instead of 200
differences.decision_ref: Known and tracked, but not decided: runbook 18.5 #14 ('Logger.SAP puede lanzar dentro de un catch si no puede crear la carpeta', closure B7 'crear carpetas'). The added log also conflicts with the 17.2 rule 'no hay logs que LAN no tenga', which was applied to InsertarSolicitudAsync but not to this controller
differences.evidence: LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:154-157; SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:37-47; SS Helpers/Logger.cs:26-31
differences.concrete_case: Guest credit order (infoCliente.cuenta='' and cliente=''): ProcessCreditPaymentAsync throws 'Los invitados no pueden pagar con crédito.' (OrderMethods.cs:677-678) and it reaches the controller catch. The SS app pool cannot create {AppBase}\Logs, so UnauthorizedAccessException escapes and SS answers 500. The DMZ PostSAP then returns 'WebException: ... Body: ...' as a 200 string to Magento, instead of 'Error, Error en SetOrder: Los invitados...'. LAN always returned 200 with e.ToString().

differences.what: The response log after processing is not on the processing host
differences.lan: :152 logs SetPedido's return (for example the account) or 'No se gener  el pedido, revisa el log SetOrder' to setOrder.log, inside the try. If that write fails after the order was created, the catch returns Ok(e.ToString()) instead of the account
differences.sap: SS does not log the response on success. The DMZ logs the SS JSON response at :197 (setOrder.log, 'SAP RESPONSE [id] ') and :198 (sap.log, 'ORDER_NEW [id] '), so the content and format differ: an SS JSON object instead of LAN's plain string. SS cannot replace a successful response with an exception text because of a log write
differences.decision_ref: None
differences.evidence: LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:152,:154-157; SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:27-35; DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:197-198
differences.concrete_case: CRED515773 succeeds. LAN setOrder.log gets '[ts] INFO [CRED515773] <cuenta>'. SS writes nothing. The DMZ writes '[ts] SAP RESPONSE [CRED515773] {"BP":"...","SalesDocument":"CRED515773","Message":"","Resultado":"Concluido"}'. Also, because ReSetPedido keeps only the first line with '] INFO [', a LAN response line matched on its own (no '{') would throw in line.Remove(0,-1). This quirk is LAN-only.

comparisons.question_for_user:
1. Is the DMZ body log the intended replacement for LAN's setOrder.log line, so this can be marked INTENTIONAL? It is at DMZ OrdersController.cs:114 (setOrder.log) and :194 (sap.log), from commit 50afd93 'Se añaden logs para los body de Magento en DMZ'. Or do you also want the body logged on ServicioSAP? If you want it on ServicioSAP, it has to be the raw request body (Request.Content), not JsonConvert.SerializeObject(order). The SS OrderRequest is typed: subTotal, total, impuesto and costoEnvio are decimal, InfoClienteRequest drops any infoCliente key it does not declare, and it adds null docType/salesOrg and similar fields plus 0 for idMagento and uen. So a serialized SS model would not match the line LAN wrote.
2. Does anyone still use LAN GET order/getOrderInfoAndSet/{incrementId} to recover failed orders? After the cutover it cannot find new orders in LAN's log. It falls back to Magento and creates the order through the legacy LAN SetPedido, which writes a credit application outside ServicioSAP. Should it be disabled, or does ServicioSAP need a replay equivalent that avoids the duplicate application (runbook 18.5 #17)?

comparisons.name: Group lines by SKU (AgruparCantidadPorSKU)
comparisons.lan_source: None. Pure in-memory transformation of the request body (List<Dictionary<string,string>> articulos). No SQL table, no SP, no config.
comparisons.sap_source: None. Pure in-memory LINQ GroupBy over the typed request body (List<ArticuloRequest>). No OData entity, no HTTP API, no config. Because neither side reads a data source, the businesspartner-dev and salesanddistribution-dev repos have nothing to check for this step.
comparisons.lan_detail:
Entry: Controllers/OrdersController.cs:137-160 [Route("setOrder")] Set(OrderRequest). It checks only order==null (:141-142), then calls om.SetPedido(order) inside a try (:151). The catch returns Ok(e.ToString()) (:156): HTTP 200 with the full exception type, message and stack. SetPedido (Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:533) calls AgruparCantidadPorSKU as its very first statement (:535). That is OUTSIDE SetPedido's own try (which starts at :575 and only logs at :727-730), so any exception reaches the controller. It runs before the forzarOrder capture (:538), ToArray (:539), the duplicate check (:541) and every write.
AgruparCantidadPorSKU (:486-526):
- Dictionary<string,int> cantidadPorSKU and Dictionary<string,float> descuentoPorSKU. Both use the default ordinal, case-sensitive comparer.
- foreach over order.articulos (:492). A null list throws NullReferenceException.
- For each line: sku = articulo["sku"] (:494), cantidad = int.Parse(articulo["cantidad"]) (:495), descuento = float.Parse(articulo["descuento"]) (:496). Both parses use the current culture; the Web.config sets no <globalization>. A missing key throws KeyNotFoundException. A null value throws ArgumentNullException. A non-integer or empty value throws FormatException. A null sku throws ArgumentNullException from ContainsKey.
- Sums with unchecked int += and float += (:498-507).
- Second pass (:510-522): for each key in insertion order, item = First(a => a["sku"] == key). It builds a new dictionary with exactly 6 keys: sku; cantidad = int.ToString(); precio, precioEspecial and condicion copied as the raw strings of the FIRST line with that SKU; descuento = float.ToString(). On net471 that format keeps 7 significant digits.
- Replaces order.articulos (:524).
Downstream consumers in the credit path:
- The detallePedido "Insertar" loop over the grouped lines (:584-599). It writes to the eCommerce detail table for every payment method, including credit.
- The credit list articulo["cantidad"]+","+articulo["sku"] (:611-615).
- order.articulos[0]["condicion"] (:632).
- LAN CreditMethods.ProductosCreditoWeb_SaveData reads only datosped indexes 14-21 and 31 (CreditMethods.cs:113-178), none of the article concatenations.
comparisons.sap_detail:
Entry: DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:107-230 setOrder. It binds to a DMZ OrderRequest whose articulos is also List<Dictionary<string,string>> (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:23), then forwards JsonConvert.SerializeObject(order) to ServicioSAP order/new (:196). ServicioSAP therefore always receives article values as JSON strings, or null. The DMZ call to LAN setOrder is commented out (:131-183).
ServicioSAP Controllers/OrderController.cs:16-48 SetOrder(OrderRequest). It checks only order==null (:20-23) and never checks ModelState: a grep for ModelState in ServicioSAP returns 0 hits, and WebApiConfig.cs registers no filters. It calls SetOrderAsync(order, "Insert") (:27). The catch logs and returns Ok("Error, " + e.Message) (:37-47), which is HTTP 200.
SetOrderAsync (Methods/Order/OrderMethods.cs:1727) opens a try (:1730) and calls AgruparCantidadPorSKU as its first operation for non-return orders (:1740). It runs before ToArray (:1741), the idempotency check (:1752) and every write. The catch at :1950-1953 rethrows as "Error en SetOrder: <msg>".
AgruparCantidadPorSKU (:87-107):
- If articulos is null or empty, it returns the order unchanged (:89-90).
- Otherwise it runs GroupBy(a => a.sku) with the default ordinal comparer, which accepts a null key. Output order follows each key's first appearance.
- New ArticuloRequest per group: cantidad = g.Sum (int; Enumerable.Sum is checked); precio, precioEspecial and condicion from g.First(); descuento = g.Sum (decimal).
- Replaces order.articulos (:105).
Typed model: ArticuloRequest.cs:5-15 (sku string, precio, precioEspecial and descuento decimal, cantidad int, condicion string). Values are bound by the Web API 5.2.7 JsonMediaTypeFormatter with Newtonsoft 12.0.2. Newtonsoft uses InvariantCulture and parses the strings "1" and "8198.0000" to int 1 and decimal 8198.0000.
Downstream consumers in the credit path:
- The credit list articulo.cantidad+","+articulo.sku (:1789-1793).
- order.articulos?.FirstOrDefault()?.condicion ?? "" in ProcessCreditPaymentAsync (:700) and in CrearSolicitudCreditoAsync (:824).
- The credit branch uses nothing else from ToArray except sDatosPedido[36] (:1797-1798).
- The credit branch writes no detail lines.

differences.what: Malformed numeric value in an article (non-integer, decimal, empty or null cantidad or descuento)
differences.lan: int.Parse or float.Parse throws FormatException or ArgumentNullException at OrderMethods.cs:495-496. This is outside SetPedido's try, so OrdersController.cs:156 returns HTTP 200 with the exception text. Nothing is written: no detallePedido, no guide, no credit application.
differences.sap: This is library behavior, not repo code (Web API 5.2.7 JsonMediaTypeFormatter logs Newtonsoft conversion errors to ModelState and continues). The property stays at its default of 0. ServicioSAP never checks ModelState (0 grep hits), so grouping sums 0 (OM:97/100). The credit list gets "0,<sku>" (OM:1792) and the flow continues: SaveGuideAsync (OM:1787), the credit application and the lines are created, and it returns Concluido with the account. NO EVIDENCE of a runtime capture confirming the binding behavior.
differences.evidence: LAN Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:495-496, :535; Controllers/OrdersController.cs:151-156. SS Models/SAP/Order/ArticuloRequest.cs:11,13; Methods/Order/OrderMethods.cs:92-102, :1789-1800; Controllers/OrderController.cs:18-35. The runbook has no decision on this; §20.3 lists a similar typed-model difference for costoEnvio as 'not applied', not decided. The real credit payloads always send integer strings (Resources/magento_payloads.md:26, :55), so this is theoretical today.
differences.concrete_case: articulos:[{"sku":"OSTE00443","cantidad":"1.0","precio":"8198.0000","precioEspecial":"0","descuento":"0","condicion":"12 M MA P INM"}]. LAN: 200 with 'System.FormatException: Input string was not in a correct format...' and nothing created. SS: credit application created with an article line of quantity 0 (or whatever the lines step does with 0), and a success response.

differences.what: Article missing one of the six keys (sku, cantidad, descuento, precio, precioEspecial, condicion)
differences.lan: KeyNotFoundException. sku, cantidad and descuento are read on every line (:494-496). precio, precioEspecial and condicion are read only on the FIRST line of each SKU (:512-520). The result is HTTP 200 with the exception text and nothing written.
differences.sap: The missing property simply keeps its default (sku null, cantidad 0, decimals 0, condicion null). This is not a binding error, so the flow continues. A missing condicion on the first line gives condicion "" at OM:700 and OM:824. The application header is then created with Condicion "", and InsertCreditArticlesAsync throws 'condicion ... no existe' (OM:875-879). The ProcessCreditPaymentAsync catch swallows that (OM:709-716), so the result is an application without lines and a success response.
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:494-496, :512-520. SS OrderMethods.cs:92-102, :700, :824, :857-879, :709-716; runbook §20.3 row 1 (the condicion throw is known, tied to decision 9). All real payloads carry all six keys (magento_payloads.md:26, :55).
differences.concrete_case: articulos:[{"sku":"OSTE00443","cantidad":"1","precio":"8198.0000","precioEspecial":"0","descuento":"0"}] (no condicion). LAN: 200 with 'KeyNotFoundException' and nothing created. SS: credit application header created with an empty condicion, no lines, and 'Concluido' plus the account returned.

differences.what: Null sku
differences.lan: Dictionary.ContainsKey(null) throws ArgumentNullException (:498). The result is HTTP 200 with the exception text and nothing written.
differences.sap: GroupBy accepts a null key and groups those lines under sku=null (OM:93). The credit list gets "1," (OM:1792) and the flow continues into application creation.
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:494, :498. SS OrderMethods.cs:92-96, :1792; InsertCreditArticlesAsync splits on ',' and requires length >= 2 (OM:917-918), so "1," passes with an empty article.
differences.concrete_case: articulos:[{"sku":null,"cantidad":"1","precio":"444.0000","precioEspecial":"0","descuento":"0","condicion":"12 M VIU P INM"}]. LAN: 200 with ArgumentNullException. SS: credit application created with an empty-SKU line.

differences.what: descuento arithmetic and format: float in LAN, decimal in ServicioSAP
differences.lan: descuento is parsed to float, summed as float, and written back as float.ToString(). On .NET Framework 4.7.1 that keeps 7 significant digits: "0.00" becomes "0", "1234.5678" becomes "1234.568", "10999.995" becomes "11000". The value feeds only detallePedido Insertar (:584-599). CreditMethods does not read it (datosped 14-21 and 31 only).
differences.sap: decimal Sum is exact and keeps scale ("0.00" stays 0.00m). In the credit branch the value is not consumed at all (only cantidad, sku and condicion are).
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:489, :496, :519, :584-599; CreditMethods.cs:113-178; WebApiMagento.csproj:16 (v4.7.1). SS ArticuloRequest.cs:13; OrderMethods.cs:100, :1789-1800. No observable effect on what the credit path writes or returns, because the SS credit branch writes no detail lines (that belongs to another step).
differences.concrete_case: Two lines of SKU X with descuento "5000.005" and "5000.005". LAN detail row gets "10000.01" (float G7). SS holds 10000.010m but writes it nowhere in the credit path.

differences.what: Integer overflow when summing cantidad
differences.lan: int += is unchecked (no CheckForOverflowUnderflow in the csproj), so a sum past int.MaxValue wraps to a negative value silently and the flow continues.
differences.sap: Enumerable.Sum(int) is checked and throws OverflowException. This is caught at OM:1950, and the response is 200 'Error, Error en SetOrder: Arithmetic operation resulted in an overflow.'
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:500; csproj has 0 CheckForOverflowUnderflow. SS OrderMethods.cs:97, :1950-1953; OrderController.cs:37-47.
differences.concrete_case: Two lines of the same SKU with cantidad "2147483647" and "1". LAN produces cantidad "-2147483648" and continues. SS returns 200 'Error, Error en SetOrder: Arithmetic operation resulted in an overflow.'

differences.what: Error body when articulos is null (or any exception in this step)
differences.lan: NullReferenceException inside AgruparCantidadPorSKU (:492). The response is HTTP 200 with e.ToString(): full type, message and stack trace.
differences.sap: The guard at OM:89-90 skips grouping, but ToArray then throws NullReferenceException at OM:222. It is wrapped at OM:1953, and the response is HTTP 200 'Error, Error en SetOrder: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.' Same outcome (200, nothing written); only the body text differs. The null guard delays the failure without changing it.
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:492; OrdersController.cs:156. SS OrderMethods.cs:89-90, :222, :1950-1953; OrderController.cs:39-46. That code comment says the choice of e.Message over e.ToString() is deliberate, but no runbook decision records it.
differences.concrete_case: {... "articulos": null ...}. LAN: 200 "System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set... at WebApiMagento.Metodos.OrderMethods.AgruparCantidadPorSKU...". SS: 200 "Error, Error en SetOrder: Object reference not set to an instance of an object."

differences.what: [ADJACENT, belongs to the ToArray and idempotency steps; typing introduced at binding] precioEspecial comparison and loss of the original forzarOrder
differences.lan: Grouping keeps precioEspecial as the raw string. ToArray compares it with the string "0" (:367, :385), so "0.00" counts as a special price and switches forzarOrder to "1". SetPedido saves forzarOrderOriginal BEFORE ToArray (:536-538) and uses it in the duplicate check (:541).
differences.sap: precioEspecial is a decimal, so ToArray compares == 0 (OM:227, :244) and "0.00" counts as no special price. SetOrderAsync does NOT save the original: ToArray (OM:1741) sets forzarOrder to "1" when any line has precioEspecial != 0, and the idempotency check at OM:1752 then reads the mutated value and skips ValidarPedidoExistenteSAPAsync.
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:536-541, :367-376, :385-393. SS OrderMethods.cs:227-237, :244-254, :1740-1752. The runbook has no decision on this. Whether the duplicate check ever matches for a CRED... incrementId is NO EVIDENCE: LAN checks Venta, SS checks the SAP order ZSD_ZMER_<id>, and the credit branch creates neither at this point.
differences.concrete_case: Credit order re-sent with forzarOrder "0" and a line with precioEspecial "6990". LAN evaluates the duplicate check with the original "0". SS sees "1" and skips the check entirely.

comparisons.question_for_user:
Grouping itself is equivalent for every real payload: it groups by exact (case-sensitive) SKU, sums cantidad and descuento, takes precio, precioEspecial and condicion from the first line, keeps first-appearance order, and runs first, before any write. The only divergence is on malformed article data. LAN rejects the whole order before writing anything: HTTP 200 with the exception text for a missing key, a non-integer cantidad or descuento, or a null sku. ServicioSAP silently defaults those values (0 / null / "") and goes on to create the credit application. Should ServicioSAP reject these inputs the way LAN does, for example by validating the articles or checking ModelState at the start of SetOrderAsync, or is defaulting acceptable?
Separately, an issue in the next step: ServicioSAP reads forzarOrder after ToArray has changed it (OrderMethods.cs:1741 then :1752), while LAN saves the original first (OrderMethods.cs:536-538). Do you want that restored for parity?

comparisons.name: Duplicate order check (PedidoExistente) - credit path of setOrder
comparisons.lan_source: Intelisis SQL: `select id from venta with(nolock) where idecommerce = @IdEcommerce` (parameterized VarChar). Connection = Connection.sCadenaConexion (Intelisis). Returned to Magento through the legacy DMZ bridge, which turned it into HTTP 409.
comparisons.lan_detail: Entry: OrdersController.Set (LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:137-160) calls om.SetPedido(order) and returns Ok(response). On an exception it returns Ok(e.ToString()) (:153-157). SetPedido (LAN Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:533): (1) AgruparCantidadPorSKU :535. (2) Saves `forzarOrderOriginal = order.forzarOrder` at :538. It does this BEFORE ToArray :539, because ToArray changes forzarOrder "0"->"1" when an article has precioEspecial != "0" (string compare, :377-378 and :394-395). (3) :541 `if (obtenerIdVenta(sDatosPedido[(int)Venta.IdEcommerce]) > 0 && (forzarOrderOriginal == "0" || order.metodoPago == PAYPAL_METHOD)) return "PedidoExistente";`. sDatosPedido[0] = order.incrementId (Enums.cs:12, ToArray :342). The SQL query always runs, whatever forzarOrder is. The check happens before anything is written: the guide is saved at :606 and the credit branch starts at :609. obtenerIdVenta (:1602-1643) looks at every Venta row with that IdEcommerce, with no Mov or Estatus filter, and returns the id of the last row. Any exception (connection, timeout) is caught (:1637-1640) and returns 0, which means "not a duplicate", so the flow goes on. Null forzarOrder: null != "0", so the check is skipped. The flow then crashes at :562 `order.forzarOrder.ToString()`, which is outside the try that starts at :576. The controller answers 200 with the exception text and no credit application is created. Caller output: the JSON string "PedidoExistente". The legacy DMZ (DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:152-157, now commented out) mapped that to HTTP 409 Conflict {error:"PedidoExistente", incrementId}. A second entry, LAN validateCredit (:455-482), runs the same SetPedido and would answer 200 {status:"PROCESANDO", cuenta:"PedidoExistente"}. Its DMZ proxy is commented out (DMZ :366-401). For credit orders (incrementId "CRED515773", forzarOrder "0", precioEspecial "0" in magento_payloads.md:26,55), the credit branch returns at :649, before crearPedido :662. So SetPedido itself never creates a Venta for a CRED id. The check can only match a Venta that the external Liberador created (LiberadorCreditoMethods.cs:40-101 gets back idVenta). Indirect evidence that such a Venta carries IdEcommerce = CRED id: UpdateCreditOrderId (:1998-2017) runs `UPDATE Venta SET IdEcommerce=@NuevoId WHERE IdEcommerce=@IdAntiguo(creditIncrementId)`. Direct evidence of what the Liberador writes: NO EVIDENCE (external service VETA_URL_LIBERADOR). Neither SP_CREDITO_WEB_DATOS (SP :172-260) nor ProductosCreditoWeb_SaveData (CreditMethods.cs:94-260) checks idMagento for duplicates.
comparisons.sap_source: S/4HANA OData SD36: GET /ZAPI_DOCVTAS_CHECK_CDS/ZAPI_DOCVTAS_CHECK?$expand=to_salesdoc_items,to_zsdt_vbak,to_zsdt_vbap&sap-client=110&$filter=PurchNoC eq 'ZSD_{docType}_{incrementId}'&$format=json. The same service is exposed as the Python route AS_GET_ListadoDocumentosVentas (salesanddistribution-dev/apps/api/routes/AS_GET_ListadoDocumentosVentas.py:43-75), which only returns d.results; the repo documents no field semantics or status filtering.
comparisons.sap_detail: Entry: OrderController.SetOrder (SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:16-48) calls SetOrderAsync(order, "Insert"). SetOrderAsync (SS Methods/Order/OrderMethods.cs:1728): AgruparCantidadPorSKU :1740, then ToArray :1741. ToArray changes forzarOrder "0"->"1" when an article has decimal precioEspecial != 0 (:236-237, :253-254). The original value is NOT saved. incrementId = sDatosPedido[0] :1742. docType = `orderRequest.docType ?? "ZMER"` (:1749; tipo is "Insert", so this is not a return). purchNoC = $"ZSD_{docType}_{incrementId}" :1750. :1752 `if ((orderRequest.forzarOrder == "0" || orderRequest.metodoPago == PAYPAL_METHOD) && await ValidarPedidoExistenteSAPAsync(purchNoC))` returns new OrderResponse{Resultado="PedidoExistente", Zidecomm=incrementId} (:1754-1759). Because of the short-circuit, SD36 is only called when the condition holds. ValidarPedidoExistenteSAPAsync (:452-464) returns documentos != null && Count > 0. On any exception it logs with Console.WriteLine and returns false ("not a duplicate"). SalesMethods.CheckDocumentExistsSD36Async (SS Methods/SalesDistribution/SalesMethods.cs:132-166) builds the filter with a string-interpolated value inside single quotes (:135), URL-encoded but with quotes not escaped. It uses the HttpClient from TokenGenerator.CreateClientS4 with a 60 s timeout (Helpers/TokenGenerator.cs:127). A non-2xx or empty body throws (:151-154), deserializes d.results into List<SaleD> (:155-157), and any error is rethrown (:162-165), so it ends up as false. The check runs before anything is written, like LAN: SaveGuideAsync is at :1788 inside the credit branch (:1786-1808). Caller output: the controller maps the result to 200 {"BP":null,"SalesDocument":null,"Message":"","Resultado":"PedidoExistente"} (OrderController.cs:28-35; Zidecomm is dropped). The current DMZ forwards it as 200 (DMZ OrdersController.cs:196, :213-219). For credit: the credit branch returns at :1802-1807, before BuildSapOrderAsync (:1848). The SS Liberador call is commented out (:719-757). Nothing in ServicioSAP ever creates a SAP document with PurchNoC 'ZSD_ZMER_CRED…'; the only writer of PurchNoC is BuildSapOrderAsync :2290 (contado and returns). So for credit orders the SD36 check can never return true today, unless an external process creates such a document: NO EVIDENCE.

comparisons.question_for_user: 1) When the Liberador creates the pedido for a credit order, does it write the CRED id (e.g. 'CRED515773') into Venta.IdEcommerce, until updateCreditOrderId renames it? The code only shows this indirectly (LAN OrderMethods.cs:1998-2017). If yes, LAN refused a CRED retry during that window and ServicioSAP never does. Should ServicioSAP dedupe credit retries on its own record, e.g. CRED_SOLICITUD_WEB_DATOS_TEMP.idMagento, or on SD36 Zidecomm once the SAP credit order exists? PLAN 18.9 leaves 'deduplicacion' undecided. 2) For a duplicate, should Magento keep receiving HTTP 409 {error:"PedidoExistente"} as the legacy DMZ sent, or does Magento accept the new 200 {Resultado:"PedidoExistente"}? (PLAN 19.2 #1 is still open.)

comparisons.name: Order SP selection (unused by credit)
comparisons.lan_source: No data source is read in this step. It sets a local variable `sp` to the name of one of two stored procedures: SP_eCommerceNuevoPed (SPsOrden/SP_eCommerceNuevoPed.sql, which can return 'Concluido' at :706, 'Incorrecto' at :709 or 'PrecioIncorrecto' at :728) or SPVTASPedidosMagento (SPsOrden/SPVTASPedidosMagento.sql, which has no PrecioIncorrecto branch). The only reader of `sp` is crearPedido (LAN OrderMethods.cs:662, which calls SqlCommand(sp) at :1246), and that is cash (contado) only. The input is OrderRequest.forzarOrder, a string (LAN Models/OrderRequest.cs:23).
comparisons.sap_source: NONE. ServicioSAP has no SP, OData or HTTP API choice that corresponds to this step. forzarOrder is a string (SS Models/SAP/Order/OrderRequest.cs:44). It is read only at OM:236 and :253 (the mutation inside ToArray), at OM:1752 (the duplicate check) and at OM:2162 (BuilAdapterReturn, which is the returns path and out of scope). OM = ServicioSap/Methods/Order/OrderMethods.cs, 3358 lines in the current working tree. No businesspartner-dev or salesanddistribution-dev service applies, because nothing is fetched.
comparisons.lan_detail:
LAN WebApiMagento/Metodos/OrderMethods.cs, SetPedido (:533).
- :538 copies forzarOrder into forzarOrderOriginal before ToArray. The comment at :536-537 explains why: ToArray changes it to "1" when there is a special price.
- :539 calls ToArray. At :377-378 and :394-395 it sets order.forzarOrder from "0" to "1" when articulo["precioEspecial"] != "0". Both comparisons use == and are null-safe, and forzarOrder is not added to the array.
- :541 runs the duplicate check. obtenerIdVenta always runs (a read-only SELECT), then it compares forzarOrderOriginal == "0", which is null-safe.
- :545-555 are the OpenPay branches, which are not entered for credit.
- :557 sets sp = "SP_eCommerceNuevoPed".
- :562 checks `if (order.forzarOrder.ToString() == "1")` and :564 then sets sp = "SPVTASPedidosMagento". Because this reads the value after ToArray, a special price in any line also selects SPVTASPedidosMagento.
- :562 is outside the try, which starts at :576. A null forzarOrder therefore throws NullReferenceException out of SetPedido before anything is written: no detallePedido (:582, :599), no SaveGuide (:606) and no credit application (:624).

For credit, the credit branch (:609) always returns at :649, before crearPedido(sDatosPedido, fTotalDescuento, sp) at :662. The catch at :728-731 plus the return at :732 also never reach crearPedido. So the value of `sp` never affects credit, and the only observable effect of the step is the null crash.

What the caller gets when the crash happens:
- setOrder (LAN Controllers/OrdersController.cs:151) catches it at :154-156 and returns `Ok(e.ToString())`: HTTP 200 with the full exception text and stack trace. The log line at :152 is skipped.
- validateCredit (OrdersController.cs:470) catches it at :477-480 and returns HTTP 500 through InternalServerError(ex).
- Other callers cannot produce a null: ReSetPedido forces forzarOrder = "1" (OrderMethods.cs:1706), OpenpayMethods.cs:274 sets "1", and getOrderInfoAndSet rewrites ":null," to ":0," (Conn/Magento.cs:390) and catches at :407-409.
comparisons.sap_detail:
ServicioSAP OM SetOrderAsync (:1728).
- :1740 calls AgruparCantidadPorSKU and :1741 calls ToArray. ToArray still changes forzarOrder from "0" to "1" when precioEspecial != 0 (OM:236-237, :253-254). precioEspecial is a decimal (SS Models/SAP/Order/ArticuloRequest.cs:9) and the comparisons are null-safe.
- There is no forzarOrderOriginal copy.
- :1752 checks `(orderRequest.forzarOrder == "0" || metodoPago == PAYPAL_METHOD) && await ValidarPedidoExistenteSAPAsync(purchNoC)`. This is null-safe and short-circuits, so the SD36 check (OM:452-463) runs only when forzarOrder is "0" or the payment is PayPal.
- There is no `sp` variable and no SP selection. The credit branch (:1785-1807) never reads forzarOrder: SaveGuideAsync at :1787, ProcessCreditPaymentAsync at :1800, then it returns Resultado "Concluido" with Zctefinal = cuentaCredito at :1802-1807. The cash path posts to ZAPI_SALESORDER_SRV (:1848-1873) for any forzarOrder value, but cash is out of scope.
- The controller (SS Controllers/OrderController.cs:17-47) maps the result to 200 {BP, SalesDocument, Message, Resultado} (:27-35). An exception becomes 200 "Error, " + e.Message (:37-46), but no exception can come from forzarOrder.

Transport: DMZ order/setOrder binds forzarOrder as a string (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:27), re-serializes the order and posts it to ServicioSAP order/new (DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:196), then returns the deserialized result (:214-219). DMZ validateCredit is commented out (DMZ OrdersController.cs:366-402), so the LAN 500 path has no counterpart. Both LAN and SS use the default Web API Newtonsoft formatter (SS App_Start/WebApiConfig.cs has no formatter change), so a JSON number 0 binds to "0" in both.

With real payloads the result is the same: both credit captures send "forzarOrder":"0" and precioEspecial "0" (magento_payloads.md:26, :55), and so do all 10 other captured payloads. LAN evaluates "0" == "1" as false, the default SP is selected and never used, and SS does nothing here. CAPTURAS_REALES_APIS.md has no forzarOrder occurrences, and Logs/sap.log (12 lines) has no order bodies, so there is NO EVIDENCE of any Magento payload with a null or absent forzarOrder.

Runbook: PLAN_EJECUCION_SP_CREDITO_A_CODIGO.md has 0 matches for forzarOrder, SP_eCommerceNuevoPed, SPVTASPedidosMagento or crearPedido, so no user decision covers this step. No text in the documents I read tried to give instructions.

differences.what: Credit order with null or absent forzarOrder: LAN crashes before writing anything, while ServicioSAP creates the credit application and returns Concluido
differences.lan: NullReferenceException at OrderMethods.cs:562 (`order.forzarOrder.ToString()`), outside the try that starts at :576. Nothing is written: no detallePedido (:582/:599), no SaveGuide (:606), no ProductosCreditoWeb_SaveData (:624). setOrder returns HTTP 200 with body e.ToString(), the stack trace (OrdersController.cs:154-156), and the log line at :152 is skipped. validateCredit returns HTTP 500 (OrdersController.cs:477-480).
differences.sap: forzarOrder is only compared with == (OM:236, :253, :1752), so there is no exception. The :1752 condition is false, so the SD36 check is skipped. The credit branch runs SaveGuideAsync (:1787) and ProcessCreditPaymentAsync (:1800), which writes the application and its lines. It returns HTTP 200 {BP: cuentaCredito, SalesDocument: null, Message: "", Resultado: "Concluido"} (OM:1802-1807, OrderController.cs:27-35), and DMZ forwards it (DMZ OrdersController.cs:214-219).
differences.evidence: LAN Models/OrderRequest.cs:23 (string, nullable); LAN OrderMethods.cs:538, :541 (null-safe), :562 (dereference), :576 (try starts after it); SS OM:1752, :1785-1807; SS OrderController.cs:17-47. The runbook has no decision on forzarOrder (0 matches). Low severity because every captured payload sends "0" (magento_payloads.md:26, :55 for credit), and DMZ keeps the value as a string (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:27). The ServicioSAP behaviour is more robust, and the difference only shows if Magento ever omits the field.
differences.concrete_case: magento_payloads.md:26 (CRED515773, omnipro_pago_credito) with "forzarOrder":null or the key removed. LAN setOrder returns 200 "System.NullReferenceException: ... at WebApiMagento.Metodos.OrderMethods.SetPedido(...)" and writes nothing. ServicioSAP order/new returns 200 {"BP":"<cuenta>","SalesDocument":null,"Message":"","Resultado":"Concluido"} and has written the guide, the credit application and its article lines.

differences.what: (Belongs to the adjacent duplicate-check step, not this one. Reported here because it is the same forzarOrder variable that step 9 reads.) The duplicate check reads forzarOrder after ToArray has changed it, where LAN reads the value saved before ToArray
differences.lan: Saves forzarOrderOriginal before ToArray (:538-539; the comment at :536-537 says this is on purpose), so a special price does not turn off the duplicate check at :541. The changed value is used only for the SP choice at :562.
differences.sap: Reads orderRequest.forzarOrder at OM:1752 after ToArray (OM:1741), which changes "0" to "1" when precioEspecial != 0 (OM:236-237, :253-254). A special price therefore skips ValidarPedidoExistenteSAPAsync.
differences.evidence: LAN OrderMethods.cs:536-541, :377-378, :394-395; SS OM:236-237, :253-254, :1741, :1752. For credit the effect is hidden. The purchNoC that ServicioSAP checks is ZSD_ZMER_CRED... (OM:1749-1750), and ServicioSAP never creates that sales order for credit, because credit returns at OM:1802 before the SAP POST at OM:1873. SD36 therefore finds nothing either way, which is runbook section 18.5 #17 ('Un reintento del mismo CRED crea otra solicitud', open, 'Fuera del fin de semana'). For cash (out of scope) this can let through a duplicate SAP order for an order with a special price; that belongs in the SetOrder audit.
differences.concrete_case: magento_payloads.md:26 with articulos[0].precioEspecial="7999" and forzarOrder "0", resent after a first submission. LAN still runs obtenerIdVenta("CRED515773") and returns "PedidoExistente" if a Venta row exists. ServicioSAP sees "1" at :1752, never calls SD36 and creates a second credit application. For credit, ServicioSAP would do the same with precioEspecial "0" because of 18.5 #17, so the mutation adds no new failure for credit.

comparisons.question_for_user: If a credit order ever arrives with forzarOrder null or missing, should ServicioSAP keep accepting it (today it creates the credit application and answers Concluido), or should it reject it the way LAN effectively did? LAN never created the application and answered HTTP 200 with the exception text. My recommendation is to keep the ServicioSAP behaviour and write it down as an intentional difference: every captured Magento payload sends "0", and the LAN behaviour is a crash, not a rule.

comparisons.name: ToArray (sDatosPedido) and forzarOrder mutation
comparisons.lan_source: No I/O. This is an in-memory transformation of the Magento JSON, bound to LAN Models/OrderRequest.cs:8-28, where every field is a string, infoCliente is a Dictionary<string,string> (:20) and articulos is a List<Dictionary<string,string>> (:19). The positions are named by the Venta enum (Models/Enums.cs:10-42). The array feeds four consumers on the credit path: (1) obtenerIdVenta, which reads the Venta table (OrderMethods.cs:1602-1643); (2) SaveGuide, which writes to SQLite (:735-754); (3) detallePedido, which calls SpVTASeCommerceDetPedidos (:963-1079); (4) CreditMethods.ProductosCreditoWeb_SaveData, which calls SP_CREDITO_WEB_DATOS and reads the array as datosped (CreditMethods.cs:94-262).
comparisons.sap_source: No I/O. This is an in-memory transformation of the typed request (Models/SAP/Order/OrderRequest.cs, InfoClienteRequest.cs, ArticuloRequest.cs), where amounts are decimal and cantidad is int. The request arrives from DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:196, which re-serializes the same string/dictionary model that LAN uses (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs). The credit path reads only two positions. [0] becomes the PurchNoC for the SD36 duplicate check (OM:1750-1752) and the key for SaveGuideAsync (OM:1787). [36] feeds the Android SMS query (OM:589-613) and the BP05MA read ZAPI_BP05MA_SRV via GetClientMaAsync (OM:631-660). The values LAN passes as datosped are now read straight from the model in CrearSolicitudCreditoAsync (OM:787-843), which calls SolicitudCreditoWebMethods.InsertAsync and writes to CRED_SOLICITUD_WEB_DATOS_TEMP. I did not need businesspartner-dev or salesanddistribution-dev: this step calls no API or OData on either side.
comparisons.lan_detail:
Entry is Controllers/OrdersController.cs:138-160, route setOrder, which calls OrderMethods.SetPedido at :533.

Before ToArray:
- :535 calls AgruparCantidadPorSKU (:486-526). It rebuilds every item with the keys sku, cantidad, precio, precioEspecial, descuento and condicion, taking them from the first occurrence of the SKU. So ToArray never meets a missing item key.
- :538 saves forzarOrderOriginal before ToArray runs at :539.

ToArray (:340-440) builds 39 strings:
- [0] incrementId.
- [1] infoCliente["cliente"] if the key exists, otherwise "0" (:346-349).
- [2..7] storeId, subTotal, total, impuesto, metodoPago, costoEnvio, copied as the raw strings.
- [8..12] comma-joined sku, precio, precioEspecial, cantidad, descuento (:363-404). Per item it tests the string item["precioEspecial"]=="0" (:368, :385). If equal, precio goes into both price slots. If not, precioEspecial goes into both slots and forzarOrder changes from "0" to "1" (:377-378, :394-395).
- [13..30] come from unguarded dictionary lookups (:406-423). Any of 17 missing keys throws KeyNotFoundException. ValidateOnlyNumbers (:442-452, Regex.Matches) throws ArgumentNullException if telefono or telefonoClienteMavi is null (:414, :423). [25] is the literal "impuesto extra".
- [31..35] metodoEnvio, cuotas, codigoRecogerSucursal, entityId, Agente.
- [36] cuenta if the key exists, otherwise "" (:429-432).
- [37] RedimirMonedero.ToString().
- [38] origen if the key exists, otherwise "" (:434-437).

Error handling: ToArray runs outside the try, which starts at :576. Any exception goes to OrdersController.cs:154-157, which returns HTTP 200 with e.ToString(). The validateCredit route (:477-481) returns 500 instead.

Who reads the array on the credit path:
- [0] is read at :541 (obtenerIdVenta together with forzarOrderOriginal, so the mutation never switches off the duplicate check), at :578-582 and by SaveGuide at :606.
- :562 reads the mutated order.forzarOrder.ToString(), but only to pick the non-credit SP. It throws NullReferenceException outside the try if forzarOrder is null.
- :572 blanks [35].
- detallePedido Limpiar/Insertar (:579-601) reads [2], [8] to [12] and [34].
- The credit branch (:609-649) passes the array as datosped (:636). CreditMethods.cs:113-178 reads [14], [15], [16], [17], [18] (as both delegacion and poblacion), [19], [20], [21] (phone digits, stripped again at :113) and [31] (metodoEnvio).
- [36] and [38] are not read on the credit path. Cuenta comes straight from infoCliente["cuenta"] at :619-620, :627 and :649; if the key is missing, KeyNotFoundException is thrown inside the try and the result is "". Origen comes from infoCliente at :646, defaulting to "PRODUCTOS MX".

Return value: infoCliente["cuenta"] (:649).
comparisons.sap_detail:
Entry is Controllers/OrderController.cs:16-47, route order/new, which calls SetOrderAsync at OM:1728.

Before ToArray:
- OM:1740 calls AgruparCantidadPorSKU (OM:87-107). It groups with the same first-occurrence rule and returns the order unchanged if articulos is null or empty.
- OM:1741 calls ToArray without saving a copy of forzarOrder.

ToArray (OM:198-292) builds 38 strings in the same order as LAN [0..37]:
- [1] is cliente only if it is not blank, otherwise "0" (OM:204-207).
- Decimals are written with ToString() (OM:210-214, :229-257).
- Per item it tests the decimal item.precioEspecial==0 (OM:227, :244). The branch bodies are the same as LAN, including the "0" to "1" mutation (OM:236-237, :253-254).
- [13..30] use infoCliente?.x ?? "" (OM:265-288). ValidateOnlyNumbers returns "" for null or blank (OM:318-322).
- [36] is cuenta ?? "" (OM:288). [37] is RedimirMonedero (OM:289).
- There is no [38]: InfoClienteRequest has no origen property.

Error handling: ToArray runs inside the try (OM:1730). The catch at OM:1950-1954 rethrows "Error en SetOrder: ...". OrderController.cs:37-47 turns that into HTTP 200 "Error, " + message. ModelState is never checked, so numbers that cannot be parsed become 0 and missing keys become null.

Who reads the array on the credit path:
- [0] becomes incrementId at OM:1742, then purchNoC at OM:1750, then the duplicate check at OM:1752, which reads the mutated orderRequest.forzarOrder. It is also used by SaveGuideAsync (OM:1787).
- [36] feeds ObtenerNumeroTablaSmsAsync (OM:1797) and IsValidatedAsync (OM:1798).
- Nothing else is read before the credit branch returns at OM:1802-1807.

The fields LAN reads from datosped now come straight from the model in CrearSolicitudCreditoAsync: Direccion :812, Exterior :813, Interior :814, CodigoPostal :816, Delegacion and Poblacion :817-818 (both from municipio), Estado :819, Colonia :820, phone digits :796, MetodoEnvio :830. These are the same fields with the same transformations; PLAN §11.3 bloque 1 reaches the same conclusion.

The uncommitted working-tree diff does not touch ToArray. It removed sDatosPedido and isValidated from the ProcessCreditPaymentAsync call (hunk @@ -1883 +1800).

Out of credit scope, for the record: the non-credit code reads two wrong positions of this array. OM:1816 reads [20] (estado) as the postal code, and OM:1919 passes [16] (numInt) as the email. Both are already listed as D-02 and D-03 in COMPARATIVA_SETORDER_LAN_VS_SAP.md.

No embedded instructions were found in the documents I read.

COMPARATIVA D-01 and MATRIZ G1-06/G5-01 already list it as open. The step description's claim of the "same forzarOrder='1' side effect" holds for the change itself, not for what happens next. comparisons.question_for_user: 1) Should ServicioSAP copy LAN on forzarOrder: save a copy before ToArray (OM:1741) and use it in the duplicate check at OM:1752, as LAN does at :538/:541? 2) LAN rejected some payloads without creating an application: a missing infoCliente key, a null phone, a null forzarOrder, or an empty or invalid precioEspecial. Should ServicioSAP also stop before OM:694 in these cases, or is its more lenient behavior acceptable? 3) Can Magento send a credit order with precioEspecial other than "0"? 4) Credit orders in SAP have nothing equivalent to LAN's SpVTASeCommerceDetPedidos staging (detallePedido Limpiar/Insertar). Is that staging needed for them, or can it be dropped on purpose?

comparisons.name: Typed binding of the Magento payload (setOrder / order/new, credit path)
comparisons.lan_source: No binding step as such. Web API 5.2.7 + Newtonsoft 12.0.3 (LAN packages.config:4,16) binds LAN Models/OrderRequest.cs:6-29: all money fields are strings (:12-18), articulos is List<Dictionary<string,string>> (:19), infoCliente is Dictionary<string,string> (:20), forzarOrder is a string (:23). Only sucursalDestino is typed (int, :22), and RedimirMonedero (float, :26). Parsing happens later in Metodos/OrderMethods.cs and Metodos/CreditMethods.cs. No SQL table or SP is involved in binding.
comparisons.sap_source: Web API 5.2.7 + Newtonsoft 12.0.2 (SS packages.config:12,32). The default JsonMediaTypeFormatter binds into typed models: Models/SAP/Order/OrderRequest.cs:5-54, ArticuloRequest.cs:3-16 and InfoClienteRequest.cs:3-80. No OData or HTTP API is involved, so businesspartner-dev and salesanddistribution-dev do not apply. Upstream, the DMZ binds Magento's body into a model identical to LAN's (DMZ Models/OrderRequest.cs:10-34), re-serializes it and posts it to order/new (DMZ Controllers/OrdersController.cs:109, :196). So ServicioSAP always receives numbers as JSON strings, and it never receives top-level fields that are missing from the DMZ model (docType, salesOrg, ...).
comparisons.lan_detail:
LAN has no typed binding. The controller (Controllers/OrdersController.cs:139-160) only guards order==null (:141-142), then logs the whole bound order (:144) and calls SetPedido (:151). Any exception becomes HTTP 200 with the exception text: `return Ok(e.ToString())` at :154-156. Nobody checks ModelState: WebApiConfig.cs:11-25 has no filters or formatter changes.

SetPedido (Metodos/OrderMethods.cs:533) parses values in this order:
1. AgruparCantidadPorSKU (:535 -> :486-526) runs outside the try. It indexes sku, cantidad and descuento (:494-496) and precio, precioEspecial and condicion (:517-520). It calls int.Parse(cantidad) (:495) and float.Parse(descuento) (:496), both using the server culture. A missing key, a null or a non-numeric value throws, and the caller gets 200 with the exception text.
2. The original forzarOrder is saved (:538). ToArray (:539 -> :340-440) runs outside the try. It indexes 17 infoCliente keys with no guard (:406-423). ValidateOnlyNumbers(null) on telefono or telefonoClienteMavi throws, because Regex.Matches(null) throws (:414, :423, :445). ToArray changes forzarOrder "0" to "1" when precioEspecial is not the text "0" (:368, :377-378, :385, :394-395). It reads cliente, cuenta and origen only through ContainsKey (:346, :429, :434).
3. The duplicate check uses the ORIGINAL forzarOrder (:541).
4. `order.forzarOrder.ToString()` (:562) is outside the try, so a null forzarOrder throws a NullReferenceException.

CreditoWeb_InsertArticulo float.Parses the SEGU00001 amount (:901) inside the inner try, whose catch returns "err" (:246-252). That return value is discarded (OrderMethods.cs:624).

comparisons.question_for_user: For this step, should ServicioSAP keep LAN's fail-fast behaviour? LAN wrote nothing when a required infoCliente or articulos key was missing, or when cantidad, descuento, total or precio was not numeric. Or do you accept the silent defaults because the DMZ always forwards well-formed strings? If ServicioSAP should reject, there are two ways: read ModelState, or wire up the existing but unused ValidarOrdenCompleta. In that case, what should Magento receive? LAN answered HTTP 200 with the exception text, or "" for errors inside the try; ServicioSAP today answers 200 "Error, ...". Also, can Magento ever send costoEnvio as "0.00", or leave forzarOrder out? Those two are the only cases where real traffic could hit the differences above (PLAN §20.3, MATRIZ G5-17).

comparisons.lan_detail:
Call site: OrderMethods.cs:582, inside the SetPedido try block (:576). It runs for every order that gets past the PedidoExistente check (:541-542) and the Openpay early exit (:545-549), so a credit order always runs it. It runs BEFORE the Insertar loop (:584-601), SaveGuide (:606) and the credit branch (:609-649).
Arguments: sOpcion="Limpiar", partidas=1, sUen=sDatosPedido[NombreTienda]=order.storeId (ToArray :349, enum Models/Enums.cs:14), sIdEcommerce=sId=order.incrementId (ToArray :344, e.g. "CRED515773" in real payloads, magento_payloads.md:26). The remaining arguments are dummies ("", "1.0", "1.0", "1", "1.0", "1", "1", 0).
detallePedido (OrderMethods.cs:963-1079):
- saResultado[0]="Incorrecto" (:969).
- switch on sUen.Trim() maps muebles_america/viu/mavi to 1/2/3, anything else to 0 (:970-981). This runs OUTSIDE the method's try block.
- iTotalArt stays 0 because the option is not "Insertar" (:983-990).
- It builds 11 SqlParameters (:998-1033): @IdMag=sIdEcommerce.Trim(), @Art="", @Precio/@Preciosesp/@Descto="1.0" as VarChar (the SP declares them float, so SQL Server converts implicitly), @Cantidad=0, @idOrden="1", @Cp="1", @RecSuc=0.
- It executes SpVTASeCommerceDetPedidos with CommandTimeout 60000 (:1036-1044).
- saResultado[0] = row["Result"] ('concluido') (:1063-1065).
- Only SqlException is caught. It is logged with Logger.SetOrder("INFO [id] ", msg) and the method returns "Incorrecto" (:1072-1075).
SP (:155-162): DELETE FROM eCommerceDetPedidos WHERE IdPedido=@IdMag AND RefPedidoIntelisis IS NULL; SELECT 'concluido' Result. Rows already bound to an Intelisis order (RefPedidoIntelisis is set by SPVTASPedidosMagento.sql:291-296 and SP_eCommerceNuevoPed.sql:423-428) survive. @UEN and every other parameter are ignored in this branch.
Caller: the return value 'deped' is never read in the credit path. It is overwritten at :599 and only read in CorreoErrorPrecio (:1324-1332). So Limpiar never changes the setOrder response: credit still returns order.infoCliente["cuenta"] (:649).
Purpose, inferred from the code: an idempotency guard for the staging table. A credit order creates no Venta during the request, so obtenerIdVenta returns 0 and a Magento retry reaches :582 again. Limpiar removes the previously staged, unbound lines so that Insertar (:599) does not duplicate them.

- UpdateCreditOrderId, which renames IdPedido CRED...→real id and sets IdOrden (:2019-2045).

- Provider.GetIdPedidoByOrden, used by setOrderStatus→CompraArtVirtual (Metodos/Order/Provider.cs:30, :108-112; Controllers/OrdersController.cs:314-333).
- SP_eCommerceNuevoPed / SPVTASPedidosMagento, cash path only (credit returns at :649 before crearPedido :662).
